brief.meaningEn: Be the person or group subjected to an action, often an unpleasant one, rather than the one doing it.
brief.meaningZh: 身處承受某行為影響的一方，通常是承受不愉快的對待，而非施行該行為的一方。
brief.grammar: Be/on the receiving end of + criticism, abuse, a decision or other action. Specify whose action and who experiences it; receiving does not imply willing acceptance.
brief.register: Everyday workplace conversation; an assistant discusses how a scheduling change felt to staff who were affected by it.
brief.boundaryZh: 須辨清行動的發出者與承受者；不代表對方同意、值得遭受或完全無法回應。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是單純收到包裹，也不等於兩方承受的後果相同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出誰作出行動、誰承受影響，以及影響是甚麼。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 177, row 10; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Harm feels different to someone on the receiving end.

listening.en: The manager announced a new rota without warning. Night staff were on the receiving end of the change: they had to rearrange childcare at short notice.
listening.zh: 經理沒有預告便宣布新更表。夜班職員承受了改動帶來的影響，須在短時間內重新安排照顧孩子。
listening.promptZh: on the receiving end 在這裏指誰？

options.en: Night staff who had to deal with the change.
options.zh: 須應付更表改動的夜班職員。

options.en: Night staff designed the new rota themselves.
options.zh: 夜班職員自行制定新更表。

options.en: The manager had to rearrange night staff’s childcare.
options.zh: 經理須重新安排夜班職員照顧孩子的事。

options.en: Night staff kept the old rota without any change.
options.zh: 夜班職員沿用舊更表，完全沒有改動。

listening.explanationZh: 經理作決定，夜班職員承受短時間內改安排的影響。

reply.promptEn: Who bore the consequences of the transport office’s sudden route change? Elderly residents had to walk farther to the new stop; the office itself did not make that walk.
reply.promptZh: （交通部門突然改路線後，誰承受後果？長者須多走一段路才能到新車站；部門本身不用走這段路。）

options.en: The elderly residents had to deal with the change.
options.zh: 長者須面對這項改動。

options.en: The people using the stop bore the practical cost.
options.zh: 使用車站的人承受實際代價。

options.en: The elderly residents were on the receiving end of the route change.
options.zh: 長者是路線改動影響所及的一方。

options.en: The transport office’s decision affected older passengers.
options.zh: 交通部門的決定影響長者乘客。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指長者承受改路線的實際影響。

scene.promptZh: 導演臨時改首映時間，主持人因此錯過返程尾班車。若說誰承受改動影響，哪句最貼切？

options.en: The host was on the receiving end of the last-minute change.
options.zh: 主持人承受了臨時改動的影響。

options.en: The host chose the new premiere time.
options.zh: 主持人決定了新的首映時間。

options.en: The director was the one who missed the last train.
options.zh: 錯過尾班車的是導演。

scene.explanationZh: 導演改時間，主持人承受無車可回的後果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不適合說某人 on the receiving end？

options.en: Residents must handle noise from a decision they did not make.
options.zh: 居民須承受一項非由自己作出的決定帶來的噪音。

options.en: A caller repeatedly insults a worker; the worker hears the insults.
options.zh: 來電者反覆辱罵員工，員工承受辱罵。

options.en: A planner independently designs a timetable but nobody is affected yet.
options.zh: 規劃者獨自設計時間表，目前尚無人受影響。

contrast.explanationZh: 尚無人承受該行動的影響。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「on the receiving end 表示當事人必定同意該安排。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Being on the receiving end identifies who experiences the action; it says nothing about consent.
options.zh: 身處承受影響的一方，只說誰經歷了該行動，沒有表示同意。

options.en: Receiving an effect is the same as approving it.
options.zh: 承受影響就等於贊成。

options.en: The phrase only concerns delivered parcels.
options.zh: 這片語只談送達的包裹。

speaking.en: When the theatre cancelled the late bus without notice, volunteers were on the receiving end of that decision and had to pay for taxis.
speaking.zh: 劇院沒有預告便取消尾班接駁巴士，義工承受了決定帶來的影響，只好付錢乘的士。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出誰作決定、誰承受車費。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學校行政處把飯堂午餐時段提前十五分鐘，沒有先通知清潔隊；清潔隊原來的工作與用膳時間重疊，被迫重新編更，但行政處沒有額外工作。用英文分辨作決定與承受影響的人。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出行政處提前十五分鐘、清潔隊未獲預告並要重編更、行政處沒有承受這項額外工作。

examples.en: The office moved lunch fifteen minutes earlier, but cleaners were on the receiving end of the unannounced change: they had to rewrite their rota when work overlapped with lunch, while the office had no extra duty.
examples.zh: 行政處把午餐提前十五分鐘，但清潔隊承受未預告改動的影響：工作與用膳時間重疊，須重編更表，而行政處沒有額外工作。

examples.en: Cleaners were on the receiving end of the office’s decision to move lunch fifteen minutes earlier. They had no warning and had to rearrange their duties; the office did not face that extra task.
examples.zh: 清潔隊承受行政處把午餐提前十五分鐘的影響。他們未獲預告，須重新安排職務；行政處本身不用處理這項額外工作。

takeaways.en: On the receiving end identifies the person who experiences another party’s action.
takeaways.zh: 身處承受影響的一方，指經歷另一方行動的人。

takeaways.en: Being on the receiving end does not imply agreement or deserved treatment.
takeaways.zh: 承受影響不代表同意，也不代表理應受此對待。

brief.meaningEn: Clearly and sharply defined, with little ambiguity; often used in a negated form for distinctions that are not simple.
brief.meaningZh: 界線清楚、容易分辨；否定形式常用於表示界線並不簡單明確。
brief.grammar: Clean-cut is a hyphenated adjective before a noun or after a linking verb. In “not clean-cut”, the distinction is unclear, not necessarily absent.
brief.register: Everyday analytical discussion; a teacher explains why two categories of public art overlap.
brief.boundaryZh: 「界線不清」不等於兩類完全相同；也不是說不能作任何判斷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是指頭髮剪得整齊的外觀意思；須看上下文中的分類界線。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出分類之間哪些部分重疊、哪些差異仍存在。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 177, row 11; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The boundary is not always clean-cut.

listening.en: The exhibition includes drawings that also use digital animation. The line between the two sections is not clean-cut, even though each has a different main focus.
listening.zh: 展覽有些畫作亦用了數碼動畫。雖然兩個展區各有重點，兩者之間的界線並不十分清晰。
listening.promptZh: not clean-cut 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: The categories overlap, so their boundary is unclear.
options.zh: 兩類有重疊，界線不夠清晰。

options.en: Every work fits exactly one section with no overlap.
options.zh: 每件作品都只屬於一個展區，毫無重疊。

options.en: The two sections share exactly the same main focus.
options.zh: 兩個展區的主要重點完全相同。

options.en: The exhibition has merged both sections into one.
options.zh: 展覽已把兩個展區合併為一個。

listening.explanationZh: 數碼動畫與畫作有交集，但兩區仍有不同重點。

reply.promptEn: Should the library separate local history from family memoirs? Some books contain both personal stories and verified town records, although other books fit one shelf clearly.
reply.promptZh: （圖書館應否把地方史與家族回憶錄完全分開？部分書兼有個人故事及經核實的城鎮紀錄，雖然另一些書可清楚放入其中一類。）

options.en: Some titles sit between the two categories.
options.zh: 部分書介乎兩類之間。

options.en: The shelving distinction has exceptions.
options.zh: 書架分類有例外。

options.en: The division is not clean-cut for every book.
options.zh: 並非每本書的分類界線都清楚。

options.en: A few books combine both kinds of content.
options.zh: 少數書同時包含兩種內容。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均承認有些書跨越分類界線。

scene.promptZh: 兩種課程大多不同，但有幾個共同單元，學生可互相認學分。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The boundary between the courses is not clean-cut.
options.zh: 兩種課程的界線不十分清晰。

options.en: Every module in both courses is identical.
options.zh: 兩種課程的每個單元都完全相同。

options.en: Students can transfer every course credit without review.
options.zh: 學生無須審核便能轉認所有課程學分。

scene.explanationZh: 有共同單元，但兩種課程並非完全相同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最能支持 clean-cut 的肯定用法？

options.en: Two award categories have separate rules and no overlapping eligible entries.
options.zh: 兩個獎項有不同規則，合資格作品完全不重疊。

options.en: Several entries meet both categories’ rules.
options.zh: 多項作品同時符合兩類規則。

options.en: Judges cannot agree which category applies to half the entries.
options.zh: 評審無法判斷一半作品適用哪一類。

contrast.explanationZh: 資格完全不重疊，界線較清晰。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「not clean-cut 等於兩類完全沒有差別。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Not clean-cut means the boundary is unclear; the categories may still differ in other respects.
options.zh: 界線不清只表示難以明確劃分；兩類在其他方面仍可能不同。

options.en: It proves all examples are identical.
options.zh: 這證明所有例子完全相同。

options.en: It describes only a neat hairstyle.
options.zh: 它只形容整齊髮型。

dialogue.explanationZh: 有重疊不代表完全相同。

speaking.en: The difference between a rehearsal and a public preview is not clean-cut when invited guests can comment and changes are still possible.
speaking.zh: 當受邀觀眾可提意見，而作品仍可修改時，排練與公開預演的界線並不十分清晰。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出觀眾做甚麼令界線變得模糊。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區中心把活動分為「運動」與「社交」。晨間健步小組既有步行鍛鍊，也有交流環節；拳擊課主要是運動，茶敘主要是社交。用英文描述分類界線，不要說兩類完全一樣。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出健步小組兩種元素、拳擊課與茶敘各有主要目的、分類界線並不完全清晰。

examples.en: The boundary is not clean-cut: the morning walking group combines exercise with conversation, although boxing is mainly sport and the tea gathering is mainly social.
examples.zh: 分類界線並不完全清晰：晨間健步小組結合運動與交流，但拳擊課主要是運動，茶敘主要是社交。

examples.en: Sport and social activities are not clean-cut categories at this centre. Walking offers both movement and conversation, while boxing is mainly sport and the tea gathering mainly social.
examples.zh: 在這個中心，運動與社交活動不是界線完全清楚的類別。健步活動兼有鍛鍊和交流，拳擊課則主要是運動，茶敘主要是社交。

takeaways.en: A clean-cut distinction has a clear boundary.
takeaways.zh: 界線清晰的區分，表示分類不易混淆。

takeaways.en: A distinction that is not clean-cut can still preserve real differences.
takeaways.zh: 界線不清，不等於兩類完全沒有差別。
